records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Limiting top-level domains to five characters rejects valid hosts such as example.technology and prevents their configuration.
records.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 a regex validation: `validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters. Valid TLDs like .museum (6 chars) or .technology (10 chars) would be rejected by this regex. records.rationale: The finding describes a real issue in the save action at line 38. When categoryId is null (no category selected), the code calls `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` which would return null/undefined. The server-side code in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb sets category_id to uncategorized_category_id when blank, but the client-side code at line 38 doesn't account for this - it directly sets the category to the result of findById(null), which would be null, causing the UI to display an empty category even though the server saved it as uncategorized.

records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — Update and delete dereference a nil record for stale or unknown IDs, turning routine admin races into HTTP 500 responses.
records.rationale:

```ruby

  host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first
  save_host(host)
end

def destroy
  host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first
  host.destroy
```

records.stripped_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — Update and delete dereference a nil record for stale or unknown IDs, turning routine admin races into HTTP 500 responses.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Interpolating stored host values without SQL quoting lets an apostrophe break the migration or injected SQL execute with migration privileges.
records.rationale: The migration at line 25 uses string interpolation to insert host values directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The variable `h` comes from splitting the legacy `embeddable_hosts` site setting value by newlines. If any host value contains a single quote (apostrophe), it would break the SQL syntax. More critically, if malicious data was stored in the site setting, it could lead to SQL injection. This is a real security/correctness bug in the migration code.
records.stripped_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Interpolating stored host values without SQL quoting lets an apostrophe break the migration or injected SQL execute with migration privileges.
